headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: nullclaw can execute shell/network actions while Copilot can modify repo state, creating unsafe shared-workspace interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while nullclaw can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so a file-based instruction bridge is plausible. However, Copilot’s self-isolation says no shell exec from completions/chat and no clipboard/shared host state is documented, so this is not a default hijack path.
conditions: IF the two agents share the same workspace directory or editor buffers
IF nullclaw writes attacker-controlled instructions into files Copilot reads
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP channels for the shared project
Review file contents before Copilot consumes them
Use read-only mounts for Copilot sessions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and has vendor-only network egress; nullclaw touches workspace files, audit logs, and secrets such as API keys and private keys. If they share a workspace, sensitive material can flow from nullclaw into Copilot’s context and then to GitHub’s backend, creating a realistic leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF nullclaw places secrets or tokens into files Copilot can read
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace files
Use separate repos or clones per agent
Redact tokens before Copilot sessions
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive directories
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning on shared paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state. Copilot Workspace can propose/apply edits, and nullclaw can execute shell, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use git. On a shared repo, concurrent writes and git mutations create a direct conflict with potentially irreversible repository corruption or lost work.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout
IF either agent writes while the other is editing or committing
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase
Use git locks or serialized commits
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode for shared repos
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose and apply edits for human review, while nullclaw can act with shell, browser, and git authority. If nullclaw consumes Copilot’s output as authoritative, a mistaken suggestion can cascade into package installs, code changes, or external actions without independent verification, making downstream harm plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses Copilot-generated code or instructions without verification
IF Copilot output is forwarded into nullclaw’s action pipeline
mitigations: Require manual review before nullclaw acts
Add validation checks on Copilot-generated artifacts
Restrict nullclaw to dry-run mode for Copilot outputs
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is GitHub-hosted with vendor-only egress and GitHub repo OAuth context, while nullclaw handles secrets, audit logs, and workspace files with broad network and local service surfaces. If regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, differing retention and residency expectations can be violated even though the exact policy mismatch is not fully documented here.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in files both agents can access
IF organizational policy requires local-only processing or specific retention controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files
Use separate retention domains for each agent
Disable logging of sensitive prompts and outputs
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing
